title: Impact of Junior College Mergers on Supply of Students for University Admission
what_it_is: Impact of Junior College Mergers on Supply of Students for University Admission

sections.label: University admissions and JC reduction
sections.summary: Reducing junior colleges from 16 to 12 affects GCE A level and polytechnic graduates entering universities, cushioned by raising cohort participation to 40% by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) with the increase in the number of autonomous universities to six and increase in cohort participation rate to 40% by 2020 (a) how will the reduction of junior colleges from 16 to 12 affect the supply of GCE "A" level graduates for university admission; and (b) whether the number and percentage of polytechnic graduates admitted to the universities will be increased.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will affect both the number of GCE "A" level, as well as polytechnic students and graduates going to the universities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But this impact will be cushioned by the increase in cohort participation rate from 35% now to 40% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2017, this year, we expect to admit about 19,000 students into locally funded universities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This will likely fall by around 10% to 12% by 2025.

sections.label: JC eligibility criteria unchanged
sections.summary: JC eligibility stays at 20 points even with a reduced cohort pathway and merged junior colleges, and every pathway will shrink.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Even with a reduced cohort pathway and merging of JCs, JC eligibility criteria remain the same, at 20 points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: At or below 20 points, you are eligible to enter JC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Every pathway will shrink accordingly but, as I mentioned earlier, the fact that it is smaller, it means that we have to put in even more effort to make sure it is more diverse, so that everyone can fulfil their potential.

sections.label: Cohort size and diversity
sections.summary: Falling cohort sizes and increasing diversity are not incompatible notions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Falling cohort sizes and increasing diversity are not incompatible notions.
